verdict.rationale: Superpowers documents its own test suites. `tests/` holds integration tests for its non-LLM code, and `evals/` is a Python harness that drives real Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI sessions, with an LLM verifier judging skill compliance. Its writing-skills method also requires pressure-scenario tests to fail and then pass for each skill. Nothing in the evidence shows these suites run on every change (CI, release gating or regression tracking), so the 'verified against regressions' part is unproven. Missing for 10: documented CI or release gating that runs the evals on every change, regression baselines or results history, and independent or hands-on corroboration that the evals are actually run.

support.subject: As a developer, the collection maintains tests or evals for its skills so changes are verified against regressions rather than shipped on vibes

citations.quote: Python harness driving real tmux sessions of Claude Code / Codex / Gemini CLI, with an LLM actor and verifier judging skill compliance.
Bash + node + python integration tests for brainstorm-server JS, OpenCode plugin loading, codex-plugin sync, and analysis utilities.
You write test cases (pressure scenarios with subagents), watch them fail (baseline behavior), write the skill (documentation), watch tests pass (agents comply), and refactor (close loopholes).
